newsitem.title: INDIA: PRESS DIGEST - Indian newspapers - July 9.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Indian newspapers - July 9.

text.p: Following is a summary of major Indian business and political stories in leading newspapers prepared for REUTERS by Business News and Information Services Pvt Ltd, New Delhi Tel:3326806, 3326813, 3326849 Fax:+91-11-3351006 E-mail: biznis@giasdl01.vsnl.net.in
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
TOP STORIES
The Times Of India
34 KILLED IN TRAIN BLAST IN PUNJAB

Thirty-four people were killed and 62 injured in a bomb explosion on a passenger train near Bhatinda in Punjab state. The dead include 10 women and 10 children. The bomb went off at about 2 p.m. in the fourth coach from the engine of the 336-Down passenger train going to Ambala from Sriganganagar. Investigators ruled out the involvement of Punjab militants in the blast but said it could be the handiwork of Kashmiri militants. Experts rummaged through the debris of the mangled carriage to identify the explosive and said the blackened faces of the victims indicated an RDX bomb.
The Hindustan Times
RIFT IN RULING UNITED FRONT

The leftist partners of the ruling United Front strongly demanded the front force Bihar state chief minister Laloo Prasad Yadav to quit his post as he could not be allowed to "disrupt" the front. The four-party Left Front said three cabinet ministers owing allegiance to Laloo Yadav's Rashtriya Janata Dal party should also quit because their party was still outside the ruling coalition. The communist parties reviewed the recent developments in the Janata Dal, the largest party in the ruling front, and announced a vigorous public campaign against Laloo Yadav.
The Economic Times
FUTURES TRADE IN CASTOR, COTTON, JUTE CLEARED

The government on Tuesday approved the globalisation of castor oil futures for a year and the revival of domestic futures trading in cotton and jute. The Bombay Oilseeds and Oil Exchange will be upgraded to an international castor oil futures exchange. Officials said this would encourage the inflow of foreign funds in domestic commodity markets and widen their resource bases. It will also help small producers receive the benefit of price stabilisation. Eighty-five percent of global exports in castor oil come from India.
CALLS CLOSE BELOW THREE PERCENT

Call rates slid to 2.75 percent towards the end of Tuesday in Bombay. The call rates, which opened at four percent, dropped to three percent with most deals taking place between three percent and four percent. While the government matched deposit growth, there is an influx of funds through external commercial borrowings and foreign investments which is building up liquidity in the system, said a banker. There are large inflows on account of redemption and interest payments expected next week.
TAX INCENTIVES FOR OIL SECTOR INVESTMENTS SOON

New overseas and domestic investments in the petroleum sector will attract major tax incentives, including a higher rate of depreciation and corporate tax concessions. A separate petroleum tax code is being discussed at the highest level. The cabinet secretary said the tax code would be based on similar codes in mature markets. Domestic government undertakings will be free from the administered price mechanism for new projects. Eliminating the administered price mechanism for future projects will allow the companies to sell oil at international prices automatically eliminating the subsidy burden, the cabinet secretary said.
Financial Express
OVER 30,000 NON-BANKING FINANCE FIRMS REGISTER WITH RBI

More than 30,000 non-banking finance companies (NBFCs) have registered with the Reserve Bank of India till Tuesday. This is 75 percent of the NBFCs that registered with the registrar of companies. On Tuesday alone 18,000 firms filed their applications. Besides the NBFCs, miscellaneous non-banking finance companies and residuary non-banking finance companies rushed to beat the Tuesday deadline. The largest number of applications, 18,000, was received in Calcutta. In Delhi about 6,000 applications were filed and in Bombay about 4,000 applications were filed for registration.
Business Standard
NEW SUPERVISORY SYSTEM FOR NON-BANKING FINANCE FIRMS

The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) has decided to introduce a differential supervisory system for non-banking finance companies (NBFCs), with tighter norms for the larger ones. It will seek monthly reports from all NBFCs with net-owned funds above 500 million rupees from this month. So far, only 10 NBFCs were filing monthly reports to the RBI. The RBI will classify the NBFCs into three groups-- with turnover above 500 million rupees, with turnover between 50 million rupees and 500 million rupees and with turnover below 50 million rupees.
The Observer
FINANCE FIRMS CROSS-DEPLOYING FUNDS

In a bid to cut their asset-liability mismatches and get a higher spread on funds, leading financial institutions are using short-term loans funds for term lending and term-lending funds to give short-term loans. Officials in leading financial institutions said this was being done due to poor credit offtake. The quarterly projections of three leading financial institutions showed that the asset-liability mismatch was bothering them. Annual cash flows are being matched with the present asset-liability situation.
MERCHANT BANKERS LOBBYING TO MANAGE DISINVESTMENT

Merchant bankers have begun lobbying to manage disinvestment of government shares in four companies. Though no time schedule for the disinvestment was proposed, it will be carried out during 1997/98 (April-March). Even without a formal invitation for any bid, merchant bankers have submitted bids to the Industry Ministry, ministry sources said.
